claims.claim: Bitdeer's structural pivot uses controlled power/data-center infrastructure as the scarce input for AI compute, converting an energy-and-site footprint originally optimized for mining into contracted GPU capacity; the fully contracted A102 facility is evidence of demand but not yet proof of realized economics.

factors.name: power-to-compute bottleneck conversion
factors.basis: controlled energized sites can shorten AI infrastructure deployment, but value capture depends on GPU availability, energization and contract economics

causalEdges.mechanism: energized infrastructure can host high-density GPUs faster than greenfield development
causalEdges.falsifier: energization/GPU deployment delays materially prevent contracted capacity from entering service

causalEdges.mechanism: customers reserve GPU capacity for compute workloads
causalEdges.falsifier: contracted capacity fails to produce durable positive gross economics

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks can migrate from power/site access to GPUs, networking, cooling, financing or customer credit quality.

unknowns.unknown: Realized margins and concentration of the new AI contracts are not established in the reused evidence.

claims.claim: The AI-infrastructure thesis remains plausible but is not validated by revenue growth alone: Q2 showed negative gross profit and a wider net loss, so contracted AI capacity must demonstrate positive unit economics rather than merely increase reported revenue.

factors.name: capital intensity and earnings-quality risk
factors.basis: rapid AI/HPC expansion occurs while consolidated gross economics are weak, raising financing and execution sensitivity

causalEdges.mechanism: facilities and GPUs require substantial capital before revenue and margins are fully realized
causalEdges.falsifier: AI capacity enters service on schedule and generates durable positive free cash flow without disproportionate financing

risks.risk: Customer concentration, GPU obsolescence, power-price exposure and financing needs can erode headline contracted-revenue value.
Bhutan expansion described as an LOI should not be treated as equivalent to contracted/operating capacity.

contradictions.claim: More than $800M expected revenue from contracted capacity is encouraging, while current consolidated gross profit is negative.
contradictions.resolution: Treat contract value as forward demand evidence, not proof of margin or cash-return quality.

unknowns.unknown: Contract tenor, customer concentration, termination protections and net cash return on GPU/facility capital require underwriting.
